NativeCommandUtcMoment.description: Real calendar date/time with seconds and an explicit Z or numeric offset; up to three fractional digits. Valid input is normalized to UTC ISO milliseconds. Local time without an offset and rolled-over calendar dates are rejected.

NotificationControls.description: Defaults are disabled for both total and category controls. Existing enabled rule definitions do not opt in. This controls only the implemented private in-App inbox; native scheduling and remote push remain unconfigured.

NotificationControlsCommand.description: expectedOwnerId restricts the actual server-derived POC owner and grants no authority. Persist the complete command/key/owner before dispatch. Authority loss/mismatch or a later parsing refusal cannot resolve an earlier uncertain commit.

NotificationSourceSnapshot.description: Retains the normalized source's original acquisition/run/expiry. dataVersion hashes the qualified normalized projection; it does not manufacture an upstream ProviderRun epoch. The default native composition remains noncommercial POC.

NotificationTriggerSnapshot.description: A same-revision/target/predicted-hour qualified false-to-true transition. The actual hour intersects both the existing astronomical dark and target windows. leadMinutes schedules relative to this interval start; missing/stale/out-of-order data and a moving window are not false measurements.

NotificationInboxMessage.description: Immutable original trigger and delivered evidence remain distinct from current qualified state. Expired, reversed or unconfirmed content must not be presented as current travel/safety advice. No OS/push delivery is asserted.

NotificationInboxPage.description: Bounded committed history read. It never waits for the global event queue to drain; processing/unavailable preserves independent existing records and does not certify absence of new notifications. checkedAt lets consumers expire current-state labels without changing original evidence.

NotificationRuleActivity.description: Live evaluation activity is separate from immutable definition/receipt markers. Arbitrary grids, score/unknown metrics, unit mismatches, unknown targets or channels have explicit unsupported reasons. Accepted events are indexed by the actual query point/target and processed in durable bounded pages; no per-rule provider polling occurs.
